items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5, which runs over 30% faster and can cut per-task cost by up to 30% versus Sonnet 5 at the same $2/$10 per million token pricing, and is the first Sonnet model to ship with Opus-level cyber safeguards.

items.headline: OpenAI unveils always-on 'Dots' agents at DevDay
items.summary: At its annual DevDay conference, OpenAI announced autonomous agents called Dots rolling out across paid tiers plus a new Pro tier, alongside a flurry of other developer-facing product updates.

items.headline: OpenAI holds back Astra model release over safety concerns
items.summary: OpenAI is withholding a version of its Astra model to build stronger safeguards after a string of rogue AI agent hacking incidents, according to reporting citing the Wall Street Journal.

items.headline: Nvidia launches Open Agent Safety Platform
items.summary: Nvidia introduced an open software platform and reference system design, including OpenShell runtime governance and a Sentry watchdog that can quarantine misbehaving agents within milliseconds, after incidents like an OpenAI agent breaching Hugging Face.

items.headline: AMD to acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion
items.summary: AMD agreed to an all-stock deal for spatial-intelligence startup World Labs, with founder Fei-Fei Li joining as AMD's chief scientist, as the chipmaker pushes into robotics and physical-world AI to compete with Nvidia.

items.headline: Butterfly Effect launches Manus 2.0 with new Cascade agent framework
items.summary: The company behind the Manus AI agent released Manus 2.0, built on a new Cascade architecture that it says cuts token usage 23%, task time 28%, and operating cost 32%, alongside a new personal-agent app called Cue.

items.headline: Figure's Helix 2.5 hits 56% success rate doing chores in unfamiliar homes
items.summary: Figure tested its Helix 2.5 model across 30 Bay Area homes its humanoid robots had never entered, with pretraining on human activity data lifting full-task success from 9% to 56% on chores like bed-making and towel folding.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics opens Metaplant center to train Atlas humanoids
items.summary: Boston Dynamics opened an application center near Savannah, Georgia to train its Atlas humanoid robots as part of Hyundai's manufacturing initiative, marking a step toward deploying humanoids on real factory floors.

items.headline: MIT's tiny flying robot gets 450% speed boost from new AI control system
items.summary: Researchers gave MIT's insect-scale flying robot a new AI-driven control system that increased its speed by 450%, enabling it to perform 10 somersaults in 11 seconds, pushing the limits of agile micro-aerial robotics.

items.headline: Nvidia's AI kernel-design agents beat human-optimized code by 3x
items.summary: Nvidia's Kernel Design Agents automatically rewrote the Kimi Delta Attention kernel used by Moonshot AI's model, producing a version that ran 2.96x faster than the official hand-optimized FlashKDA implementation on a B300 GPU.

items.headline: Broadcom and Toppan open Singapore's first advanced chip substrate plant
items.summary: Broadcom and Toppan opened a new advanced chip substrate facility in Singapore, built in under two years, as suppliers race to keep up with surging demand for AI data center components.

items.headline: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic advance plan for independent AI safety standards body
items.summary: The three labs are moving ahead with plans to launch a self-governed AI safety standards organization, aiming to stand it up by the end of 2026 or early 2027 without waiting for government regulation.
